first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A guide to getting married in Portugal: pick a region, check the legal rules for your passport, and talk to one Wedded Advisor who plans it. The headline is about palaces and cliffs, which sounds big and fancy, but the quick answer under it gets straight to whether we can legally marry there, which is what I care about.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Palace makes me think 200 guests and a ballroom. But the next lines, a civil process for foreign couples 'organised at least one month before the date' and 'many couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home', are exactly the kind of plain answer I was hoping for. 'Check the rules for your passport' is the button I'd tap.

attention_map.quote: What are you celebrating? Wedding, elopement, vow renewal...
attention_map.why: Seeing 'elopement' as an option and an 'under 30' guest band right near the top is the first sign small groups are welcome. It's only a picker though, it doesn't tell me anything back.

attention_map.quote: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.why: Pretty palaces and wine terraces. Nice, but on my phone I'm scrolling past looking for numbers and guest sizes.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: Nearest airport on every card is great, we want something close to an airport. But the Guests line is left out or says 'Ask your Wedded Advisor', and that is the one line I scan for first. No drive times either, so 'close to the airport' is still a guess.

attention_map.quote: events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: Good to know honestly, but a palace isn't really us.

attention_map.quote: a Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own
attention_map.why: This answers my family's question directly. A church option listed alongside quintas and beaches.

attention_map.quote: fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum
attention_map.why: So there are minimums, but no idea how much. 'Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms' is exactly my fear with only close family. It tells me the trap exists without telling me if we'd fall into it.

attention_map.quote: witnesses may take part but are not mandatory
attention_map.why: Finally, the documents and witnesses question answered with official sources: birth certificate, certificate of capacity, no translation for English documents, four numbered steps. This is the part I was most confused about and it's laid out clearly for my passport.

attention_map.quote: for about 100 guests: total EUR 25,000 to 70,000
attention_map.why: The only cost band is for 100 guests, and it may not even show. Nothing for 10 or 20 people. I can't work out what our small wedding would cost from this.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch
attention_map.why: This is a big three-day production. We want something simple. Nothing here shows what a small version looks like.

attention_map.quote: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.why: The heading hints at a small option, but the content is about transfers and quinta rooms for lots of guests.

attention_map.quote: ceremony type (legal in Portugal, Catholic, symbolic, not sure)
attention_map.why: One person from first enquiry to the day is what I need since I don't know where to start. But nothing says they will actually sort the documents and witnesses for us, only that the page explains the rules.

attention_map.quote: Is a Catholic or symbolic ceremony legal in Portugal?
attention_map.why: Useful repeats of the legal answers. No FAQ about small weddings or elopements, or a minimum spend.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: 'elopement' and an 'under 30' band in the qualifier bar suggest yes, but there are no packages at all, region cards carry no guest line, the cost table is 'about 100 guests' only, and the weekend section reads as a full production.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: The rules are explained very well by passport, with 'witnesses may take part but are not mandatory' and four numbered steps. But nothing says Wedded Concierge does the paperwork for us; it reads like a guide, not 'we handle it'.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: 'fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum' with no figure; the brief states 'No Wedded Wonderland figure' and costs may show 'no figures' until sign-off.

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'a Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own' in s4, FAQ 3, and Catholic is an option on the enquiry form.

objections_triggered.objection: Minimum guest numbers or spend that don't fit a small group
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum' and 'exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms', with no figures and nothing for small groups
No minimum spend stated anywhere; costs fall back to 'offer a Wedded Advisor estimate'
'about 100 guests' cost band, 'late party, Sunday brunch' weekend, palace hero headline
Mostly calmed by the Marrying legally tab with official sources; still unclear whether they handle it for us

trust_signals_noticed: Clear legal steps with official sources (justica.gov.pt, smartraveller, gov.uk) and a 'checked October 2026' line
'Elopement' option and an 'under 30' guest band in the qualifier
Nearest airport code on every region card
Catholic ceremony confirmed as legally recognised
Honest notes like palace dates being cancelled for state events and roof works at Monserrate
turn_offs_noticed: Cost shown only at about-100-guest scale
Wedding weekend described as a multi-day production with a late party
No guest range on any region card

emotional_response.overall: Relieved on the legal side, uneasy on size and money
emotional_response.detail: I finally understand the documents and witnesses. But I still feel like the page is for bigger weddings than ours, and I'd be going into a call not knowing if we're too small to bother with.

payload.decision_reason: The legal side is the clearest I've seen and Catholic is fine, so Portugal stays on the list. But I scan for minimums and guest ranges first and there are none: no small-group cost, no minimum spend, no guest line on the region cards, and the weekend looks like a big production. Small groups aren't clearly welcome yet, so I'd save it and compare before enquiring.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, the paperwork bit is really helpful, witnesses aren't even required, good. But we're 20 people, max 30. Every number on here is for 100 guests, and it says venues charge 'per guest with a minimum' without saying what the minimum is. I don't want to find out on a call that we're too small. Saving this one, I'll look again once I've seen what Italy or Crete say about small weddings.
